For every \(0<h\le h_0\), the maximal cardinality of an \(h\)-separated subset of \(\mathcal B\) lies in \([c_{\mathcal B}h^{-1},C_{\mathcal B}h^{-1}]\) for fixed \(0<c_{\mathcal B}\le C_{\mathcal B}<\infty\).

novel.justification: This project-specific global entropy condition is satisfied by smooth compact administrative boundaries, including the circular witnesses, and directly controls the number of boundary locations that every covering and chaining upper bound must handle; it imposes no local Ahlfors measure condition.

assumptions.condition: For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(|g_{t,P}(z)-g_{t,P}(z')|\le Ld(z,z')\) for all \(z,z'\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\) with \(\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z,x)\vee\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z',x)\le h_0\).

assumptions.condition: For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(\mathcal L_P(Y-g_{t,P}(X)\mid X=z)=\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\) for \(P_X\)-almost every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\).
\(q_{t,P}(x,h)\ge c_m h^{\kappa}\) for every \(x\in\mathcal B\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(0<h\le h_0\).

novel.justification: The common two-sided boundary modulus is project-specific and is realized by geographic designs whose score density vanishes polynomially with inward normal distance along an administrative boundary; Gaiffas2005Degenerate motivates polynomial design degeneracy only in a one-dimensional pointwise problem.

assumptions.condition: \(\mathsf J_P(h,u)\le C_{\mathrm{iso}}\{1+h^{-1}(u/h^2)^{1/(\kappa-2)}\}\) for every \(0<h\le h_0\) and \(C_mh^{\kappa}\le u\le1\).

novel.justification: The envelope is realized by a single polynomial density zero on an otherwise positive tubular design and formalizes isolated geographic access bottlenecks without restricting response smoothness.
A persistent isolated thin site occurs where a smooth boundary meets one lake, pass, or data-redaction pocket, and the circular witness gives an explicit law with this property.

Boundary-wide sampling depletion arises when residence or measurement density vanishes with normal distance from an entire administrative border, and the symmetric tubular witness realizes the condition exactly.

assumptions.condition: \(q_{t,P}(x,h)\ge m(h)\) for every \(x\in\mathcal B\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(0<h\le h_0\).

novel.justification: A declared common modulus records the weakest two-sided local information available along the boundary and can be estimated from score-only pilot data in geographic designs.

assumptions.condition: \(\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\le\mathsf J_P(h,u)\) for every \(0<h\le h_0\) and \(0\le u\le1\).

novel.justification: A lower packing envelope describes guaranteed multiplicity of sparse boundary segments and is directly realized by repeated tubular depletion.

assumptions.condition: \(\mathsf J_P(h,u)\le\mathsf J_{+}(h,u)\) for every \(0<h\le h_0\) and \(0\le u\le1\).

novel.justification: An upper packing envelope limits how many separated data deserts occur at each severity level and is satisfied by designs with finitely many cusps or boundary-wide regular depletion.

definitions.name: nonempty triangular profile union
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)=\bigcup_{(\kappa,\mathsf J_{-},\mathsf J_{+})\in\Lambda_n}\{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}:\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\le\mathsf J_P(h,u)\le\mathsf J_{+}(h,u)\text{ for every }0<h\le h_0\text{ and }0\le u\le1\}\). The declared domain of \(\Lambda_n\) requires this union to be nonempty.

definitions.name: empirical one-sided counts
definitions.construction: \(N_{t,n}(x,h)=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le h\}\) for \(x\in\mathcal B\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(h\in\mathcal H_n\).

definitions.name: count-adaptive bandwidth
definitions.construction: For \(x\in\mathcal B\), let \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)\) be the numerically smallest element of \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{h\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)}[Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\log(e+nh^{-1})/\{N_{t,n}(x,h)\vee1\}}]\) when \(\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)\ne\varnothing\), and set \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)=h_0\) when \(\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)=\varnothing\).

definitions.name: mass-adaptive boundary trace estimator
definitions.construction: \(\widehat\tau_n(x)=\widehat g_{1,n}(x;\widehat h_{1,n}(x))-\widehat g_{0,n}(x;\widehat h_{0,n}(x))\) for \(x\in\mathcal B\).

definitions.name: expected-sup minimax risk
definitions.construction: For a nonempty law class \(\mathcal P\), \(R_n(\mathcal P)=\inf_{\widetilde\tau_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widetilde\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|]\), where the infimum is over estimators measurable in \(\mathcal D_n\) and the known assignment geometry.

definitions.name: explicit circular thinning witnesses
definitions.construction: Set \(\mathcal B=S^1\), \(\mathcal A_1=\{z:\rho(z)\le0\}\), and \(\mathcal A_0=\{z:\rho(z)>0\}\). On the symmetric support \(\mathcal T\), define \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}(z)=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T}(z)|\rho(z)|^{\kappa-2}/\int_{\mathcal T}|\rho(w)|^{\kappa-2}\,dw\) and \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}(z)=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T}(z)\min\{1,(d(z,x_{\star})/h_0)^{\kappa-2}\}/\int_{\mathcal T}\min\{1,(d(w,x_{\star})/h_0)^{\kappa-2}\}\,dw\). The law \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}\) gives \(X\) density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\), independent \(Z_0,Z_1\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), and \(Y(t)=\sigma Z_t\); define \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}\) identically with density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\). Both laws have \(g_{t,P}\equiv0\) and \(\theta_{t,P}\equiv0\) for \(t=0,1\).

definitions.name: two-sided scale-dependent tent family
definitions.construction: For \(0<h\le h_0/6\), enumerate \(\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}=\{x_1,\ldots,x_{|\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|}\}\), set \(\psi_{j,h}(z)=(1-d(z,x_j)/h)_+\), and set \(\psi_{0,h}\equiv0\). Under \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{perv}}\), keep score density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) and set \(Y(1)=(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(X)+\sigma Z_1\) and \(Y(0)=-(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(X)+\sigma Z_0\). Define \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,0,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,1,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) by the same formulas with score density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\), \(\psi_{0,h}\equiv0\), and \(\psi_{1,h}(z)=(1-d(z,x_{\star})/h)_+\). In each family, \(g_{1,P}(z)=(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(z)\), \(g_{0,P}(z)=-(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(z)\), \(\theta_{1,P}(x)=(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(x)\), and \(\theta_{0,P}(x)=-(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(x)\).

definitions.name: arbitrary-modulus optimal-recovery handle
definitions.construction: Condition on the observed scores, solve the convex minimax linear-weight problem over side-specific Lipschitz biases and empirical counts, and pair its dual extremal tapers with multiscale packings bracketed by \(\mathsf J_{-}\) and \(\mathsf J_{+}\) inside the named class \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-},\mathsf J_{+})\).

definitions.name: thickness-adaptive honest-band handle
definitions.construction: Studentize the count-adaptive observed-side fits conditionally on the scores, add the exact worst-case Lipschitz bias at each selected scale, and calibrate the boundary--bandwidth supremum by a conditional Gaussian multiplier process; for adaptation limits, test benchmark-separated profile components using score-only likelihood ratios and total-variation separation.

statements.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the restriction of the observed conditional-regression equivalence class under \(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t}\) to \(\{z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}:\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z,x)<h_0\}\) has exactly one representative obeying the \(L\)-Lipschitz inequality there, namely the restriction of \(g_{t,P}\). Every \(x\in\mathcal B\) belongs to each \(\mathcal X_{t,P}\), and
\[
\theta_{t,P}(x)=\lim_{z\to x,\ z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}}g_{t,P}(z)=g_{t,P}(x)
\]
exists uniquely. Consequently the near-boundary restriction of \(g_{t,P}\), \(\theta_{t,P}\), and \(\tau_P\) are functionals of the observed law: two laws inducing the same law of \(O\) under the known assignment geometry induce the same three objects. On the intersection of \(\mathcal A_t\cap\{z:\mathbf 1\{z\in\mathcal A_1\}=t\}\) with the open \(h_0\)-tube, consistency implies that the near-boundary representative agrees, \(P_X\)-almost everywhere, with the conditional mean of \(Y(t)\) under the law normalized to that intersection whenever it has positive \(P_X\)-mass; when it has zero mass the compatibility assertion is vacuous. In particular, when the known assignment regions form the sharp partition \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), this compatibility holds \(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t}\)-almost everywhere in the open \(h_0\)-tube; this supplies the local potential-outcome interpretation without assigning a conditional mean at a null boundary point or requiring integrability of the counterfactual away from its observed side.
statements.justification: This proposition makes the target a unique observed-side trace rather than a version-dependent conditional mean at a null boundary point.
statements.gap: HahnToddVanDerKlaauw2001 identifies regression-discontinuity limits under continuity, while CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance studies the boundary curve; this node records identification on vanishing-support sides without assigning a conditional mean at the boundary itself.
statements.consumer: The \(\texttt{rd2d}\) workflow can interpret the fitted jump as an observed-law-identified causal trace contrast even when the score has zero density on the boundary.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  Define the finite Borel measure
\[
\mu_t(E):=P_X(E\cap\mathcal A_t),\qquad E\subseteq\mathbb R^2\text{ Borel}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{def:base\text{-}thickness\text{-}class}\), every assumption in that definition holds for \(P\).
The positive lower bound in \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\) implies that \(\mathcal B\) is nonempty, and \(\mathcal B\) is compact by its declared space.

We first show that every boundary point is in the support of each one-sided measure.  Fix \(x\in\mathcal B\) and \(r>0\), and set
\[
h:=\min\{h_0,r/2\}.
\]
Since \(h_0>0\), one has \(0<h\le h_0\) and \(h<r\).  The conditions \(c_m>0\) and \(\kappa>2\), together with \(\mathrm{ass:polynomial\text{-}lower\text{-}mass}\), therefore give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mu_t\bigl(\{z:d(z,x)<r\}\bigr)
&\ge P\{X\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X,x)\le h\}\\
&=q_{t,P}(x,h)\\
&\ge c_mh^{\kappa}>0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus every open neighborhood of \(x\) has positive \(\mu_t\)-mass.  By the definition of the support of a Borel measure,
\[
x\in\operatorname{supp}(\mu_t)=\mathcal X_{t,P}.
\]
This holds for every \(x\in\mathcal B\) and both values of \(t\).

Put
\[
\delta_{\mathcal B}(z):=\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z,x),
\qquad
U_{t,P}:=\{z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}:\delta_{\mathcal B}(z)<h_0\}.
\]
The triangle inequality implies
\[
|\delta_{\mathcal B}(z)-\delta_{\mathcal B}(z')|\le d(z,z'),
\]
so \(U_{t,P}\) is relatively open in \(\mathcal X_{t,P}\).  Moreover, \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\) implies, for \(P_X\)-almost every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\),
\[
\mathcal L_P\bigl(Y-g_{t,P}(X)\mid X=z\bigr)=\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2).
\]
The centered Gaussian law has finite first moment and mean zero.  Consequently
\[
\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=z]=g_{t,P}(z)
\]
for \(P_X\)-almost every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), and hence for \(\mu_t\)-almost every such \(z\).  Thus \(g_{t,P}|_{U_{t,P}}\) is a representative of the observed-outcome conditional-regression equivalence class restricted to \(U_{t,P}\).  By \(\mathrm{ass:lipschitz\text{-}side\text{-}means}\),
\[
|g_{t,P}(z)-g_{t,P}(z')|\le Ld(z,z'),
\qquad z,z'\in U_{t,P},
\]
so this representative obeys the required inequality.

We next prove pointwise uniqueness.  Let \(f_1,f_2:U_{t,P}\to\mathbb R\) be two \(L\)-Lipschitz representatives of the same restricted conditional-regression class.  Then
\[
f_1=f_2\qquad\mu_t\text{-almost everywhere on }U_{t,P}.
\]
Suppose, to obtain a contradiction, that some \(z\in U_{t,P}\) satisfies
\[
\Delta:=|f_1(z)-f_2(z)|>0.
\]
Because \(L>0\) and \(\delta_{\mathcal B}(z)<h_0\), choose
\[
0<r<\min\left\{h_0-\delta_{\mathcal B}(z),\frac{\Delta}{4L}\right\}.
\]
The one-Lipschitz inequality for \(\delta_{\mathcal B}\) yields
\[
B(z,r)\cap\mathcal X_{t,P}\subseteq U_{t,P}.
\]
For every \(z'\) in this relative ball, the triangle inequality and the two Lipschitz bounds give
\[
\begin{aligned}
|f_1(z')-f_2(z')|
&\ge \Delta-|f_1(z')-f_1(z)|-|f_2(z')-f_2(z)|\\
&\ge \Delta-2Ld(z,z')\\
&>\frac{\Delta}{2}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The complement of \(\operatorname{supp}(\mu_t)\) is a union of open \(\mu_t\)-null sets.  Because \(\mathbb R^2\) has a countable base, that complement is a countable union of such sets and therefore is \(\mu_t\)-null.  Since \(z\in\operatorname{supp}(\mu_t)\), it follows that
\[
\mu_t\bigl(B(z,r)\cap\mathcal X_{t,P}\bigr)
=\mu_t\bigl(B(z,r)\bigr)>0.
\]
The preceding strict separation between \(f_1\) and \(f_2\) thus holds on a set of positive \(\mu_t\)-mass, contradicting their almost-everywhere equality.  Hence \(f_1=f_2\) pointwise on \(U_{t,P}\), and the unique \(L\)-Lipschitz representative is \(g_{t,P}|_{U_{t,P}}\).

Now fix \(x\in\mathcal B\).  The support argument above gives \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), and \(\delta_{\mathcal B}(x)=0<h_0\), so \(x\in U_{t,P}\).  If \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\) and \(z\to x\), then eventually \(d(z,x)<h_0\), whence \(z\in U_{t,P}\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:lipschitz\text{-}side\text{-}means}\) gives
\[
|g_{t,P}(z)-g_{t,P}(x)|\le Ld(z,x)\longrightarrow0.
\]
By the definition of \(\theta_{t,P}\),
\[
\theta_{t,P}(x)
=\lim_{z\to x,\ z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}}g_{t,P}(z)
=g_{t,P}(x).
\]
This proves existence of the trace, while uniqueness follows from the pointwise uniqueness of the near-boundary representative.

To verify observed-law identification, let \(P\) and \(P'\) be two class members inducing the same law of \(O=(Y,X)\) under the same known assignment geometry.  Their score marginals coincide, so their restricted measures \(\mu_t\) and supports \(\mathcal X_{t,P}\) coincide.  Their observed conditional-regression equivalence classes also coincide because those classes are determined by the common joint law of \((Y,X)\).  Under each law, the preceding Gaussian-error argument shows that \(g_{t,P}\), respectively \(g_{t,P'}\), represents this common observed regression class on the common side support.  Pointwise uniqueness therefore gives
\[
g_{t,P}|_{U_{t,P}}=g_{t,P'}|_{U_{t,P'}}.
\]
Taking the boundary limits already established yields \(\theta_{t,P}=\theta_{t,P'}\).  Finally, the definition \(\tau_P=\theta_{1,P}-\theta_{0,P}\) yields \(\tau_P=\tau_{P'}\).  Thus the near-boundary side regressions, the boundary traces, and their contrast are functionals of the observed law; this argument never selects a version of a conditional mean at a null boundary point.

It remains to establish the stated potential-outcome compatibility.  Define
\[
S_t:=\mathcal A_t\cap\{z:\mathbf 1\{z\in\mathcal A_1\}=t\},
\qquad
D_t:=S_t\cap\{z:\delta_{\mathcal B}(z)<h_0\}.
\]
Because \(D_t\subseteq\mathcal A_t\) and \(\mu_t\) is concentrated on its support,
\[
P_X(D_t\setminus U_{t,P})=0.
\]
Hence, for each \(z\in U_{t,P}\), there is \(x_z\in\mathcal B\) such that
\[
d(z,x_z)=\delta_{\mathcal B}(z)<h_0.
\]
The boundary-support result, the trace identity, \(\mathrm{ass:bounded\text{-}side\text{-}traces}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:lipschitz\text{-}side\text{-}means}\) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
|g_{t,P}(z)|
&\le |g_{t,P}(x_z)|+Ld(z,x_z)\\
&=|\theta_{t,P}(x_z)|+L\delta_{\mathcal B}(z)\\
&\le L(1+h_0).
\end{aligned}
\]
If \(Z\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\), direct integration gives
\[
\mathbb E|Z|
=\frac{2}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_0^{\infty}u\exp\left(-\frac{u^2}{2\sigma^2}\right)\,du
=\sigma\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}.
\]
Therefore \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), the preceding envelope, and \(P_X(D_t\setminus U_{t,P})=0\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_P\bigl[|Y|\mathbf 1\{X\in D_t\}\bigr]
&\le \mathbb E_P\bigl[|g_{t,P}(X)|\mathbf 1\{X\in D_t\}\bigr]
+\mathbb E_P\bigl[|Y-g_{t,P}(X)|\mathbf 1\{X\in D_t\}\bigr]\\
&\le \left\{L(1+h_0)+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}\right\}P_X(D_t)<\infty.
\end{aligned}
\]
On \(\{X\in D_t\}\), the definition of \(S_t\) and \(\mathrm{ass:sharp\text{-}assignment}\) give \(T=t\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:consistency}\) then gives \(Y=Y(t)\) there, so \(Y(t)\mathbf 1\{X\in D_t\}\) is integrable.

Let \(p_t:=P_X(D_t)\).  If \(p_t>0\), define the normalized law
\[
Q_t(C):=\frac{P(C\cap\{X\in D_t\})}{p_t}.
\]
For every bounded Borel function \(b:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R\), the observed-regression identity proved from \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), followed by \(Y=Y(t)\) on \(\{X\in D_t\}\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_{Q_t}\bigl[b(X)\{Y(t)-g_{t,P}(X)\}\bigr]
&=\frac{1}{p_t}\mathbb E_P\bigl[b(X)\mathbf 1\{X\in D_t\}\{Y(t)-g_{t,P}(X)\}\bigr]\\
&=\frac{1}{p_t}\mathbb E_P\bigl[b(X)\mathbf 1\{X\in D_t\}\{Y-g_{t,P}(X)\}\bigr]\\
&=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
All terms are integrable by the bounds above, and division is valid because \(p_t>0\).  The defining characterization of conditional expectation now yields
\[
\mathbb E_{Q_t}[Y(t)\mid X]=g_{t,P}(X),
\qquad Q_t\text{-almost surely}.
\]
Equivalently, this equality holds \(P_X\)-almost everywhere on \(D_t\).  If \(p_t=0\), the almost-everywhere compatibility assertion on \(D_t\) is vacuous.

Finally, if \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), then
\[
S_0=\mathcal A_0,
\qquad
S_1=\mathcal A_1.
\]
Hence \(D_t=\mathcal A_t\cap\{z:\delta_{\mathcal B}(z)<h_0\}\), and the compatibility just proved holds \(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t}\)-almost everywhere throughout the open \(h_0\)-tube.  Because the normalization and integrability arguments used only \(Y(t)\mathbf 1\{X\in D_t\}\), no integrability of the counterfactual away from its observed side is required.

statements.statement: For every \(\kappa>2\), there are constants \(0<c_\kappa<C_\kappa<\infty\) such that \(c_\kappa h^{\kappa}\le\operatorname{Leb}_2(\mathsf H_{\kappa}\cap B(0,h))\le C_\kappa h^{\kappa}\) for all sufficiently small \(h\). In particular, the local-mass exponent is \(\kappa\), not \(\kappa-1\).
statements.justification: This calculation is the geometry kill test on which every polynomial-thickness rate depends.
statements.gap: Gaiffas2005Degenerate calibrates rates to a one-dimensional design density, while CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance does not calculate polynomial horn mass.
statements.consumer: Support diagnostics for geographic boundary designs can translate a measured horn cross-section into the correct effective-sample-size exponent.
statements.proof_tex:
By \(\mathrm{def:polynomial\text{-}horn}\), a vertical section at inward coordinate \(u\) has length \(2u^{\kappa-1}\). Since \(B(0,h)\subset\{0<u<h\}\times[-h,h]\), direct integration of these nonnegative section lengths gives
\[
 \operatorname{Leb}_2(\mathsf H_{\kappa}\cap B(0,h))
 \le 2\int_0^h u^{\kappa-1}\,du=\frac{2}{\kappa}h^{\kappa}.
\]
For \(0<u<h/2\), one has \(h^2-u^2\ge3h^2/4\). Because \(\kappa>2\), for all sufficiently small \(h<h_0\), \(u^{\kappa-1}\le(h/2)^{\kappa-1}\le\sqrt3h/2\). Hence the entire section \(\{|v|\le u^{\kappa-1}\}\) lies in \(B(0,h)\), and therefore
\[
 \operatorname{Leb}_2(\mathsf H_{\kappa}\cap B(0,h))
 \ge2\int_0^{h/2}u^{\kappa-1}\,du
 =\frac{2^{1-\kappa}}{\kappa}h^{\kappa}.
\]
Taking \(c_\kappa=2^{1-\kappa}/\kappa\) and \(C_\kappa=2/\kappa\) proves both inequalities and shows that the exponent is \(\kappa\), rather than \(\kappa-1\).

statements.statement: Under the circular inside--outside assignment in \(\mathrm{def:circular\text{-}thinning\text{-}witnesses}\), there exist fixed \(0<c_m<C_m<\infty\) such that, for every \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) and \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\). Uniformly in \(x\in S^1\), the pervasive witness has \(q_{t,P}(x,h)\asymp h^{\kappa}\) on both sides and \(\mathsf J_P(h,C_mh^{\kappa})\asymp h^{-1}\). The isolated witness has \(q_{t,P}(x_{\star},h)\asymp h^{\kappa}\) on both sides, a thin arc of length \(O(h)\), \(\mathsf J_P(h,C_mh^{\kappa})\asymp1\), and the full upper profile in \(\mathrm{ass:isolated\text{-}thin\text{-}profile\text{-}upper}\). Both witnesses have \(g_{t,P}\equiv0\) and \(\theta_{t,P}\equiv0\) for \(t=0,1\).
statements.justification: The explicit circular laws prove nonemptiness and make the same-modulus, different-multiplicity comparison a legal within-model construction.
statements.gap: Gaiffas2009Uniform and AntoniadisPenskySapatinas2014 analyze finitely many zeros in univariate regression, but neither supplies two symmetric assignment sides or a boundary-wide circular depletion witness.
statements.consumer: Simulation modules for \(\texttt{rd2d}\) can reproduce both designs from normalized score densities rather than relying on an informal horn sketch.
statements.proof_tex:
Write a point of the circular tube as
\[
 z=(1+s)(\cos\phi,\sin\phi),\qquad |s|\le h_0,quad 0\le\phi<2\pi .
\]
Because \(h_0<1\), these are nonsingular coordinates with area element \((1+s)\,ds\,d\phi\).  Hence the normalizing constant in \(\mathrm{def:circular\text{-}thinning\text{-}witnesses}\) is
\[
 Z_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
 =2\pi\int_{-h_0}^{h_0}|s|^{\kappa-2}(1+s)\,ds
 =\frac{4\pi}{\kappa-1}h_0^{\kappa-1}.
\]
It is positive and finite, uniformly away from zero and infinity for \(2<\kappa\le\overline\kappa\).  The isolated integrand is nonnegative, bounded by one, and positive off the single point \(x_{\star}\); compactness of \(\mathcal T\) and continuity in \(\kappa\in[2,\overline\kappa]\) therefore give the same uniform positivity and finiteness for its normalizer.

On a sufficiently small coordinate patch about any \(x\in S^1\), let \(s\) be signed normal depth and \(v\) signed arclength.  Compactness of \(S^1\), together with \(h_0<1\), supplies constants independent of \(x\) and \(\kappa\) for which the Jacobian is bounded above and below and
\[
 c(s^2+v^2)^{1/2}\le d(z,x)\le C(s^2+v^2)^{1/2}.
\]
Consequently, on either assignment side and for all sufficiently small \(h\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 q_{t,P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}}(x,h)
 &\asymp \int_0^h\int_{-\sqrt{h^2-s^2}}^{\sqrt{h^2-s^2}}
 s^{\kappa-2}\,dv\,ds\\
 &=h^{\kappa}\int_0^1 2w^{\kappa-2}\sqrt{1-w^2}\,dw
 \asymp h^{\kappa}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{1}
\]
The last integral is positive and is bounded above and below uniformly on the compact exponent interval.  By compactness and positivity, the constants can be enlarged so that (1) holds for every \(0<h\le h_0\).  Choose \(c_m>0\) below the uniform lower constant and \(C_m>c_m\) above the uniform upper constant.  Every boundary point then belongs to the thin set at level \(C_mh^{\kappa}\).  If \(E\) is a maximal \(h\)-separated subset of \(S^1\), the arcs of radius proportional to \(h\) about points of \(E\) are disjoint while arcs with twice that radius cover the circle.  Comparison with its arclength \(2\pi\) gives
\[
 c h^{-1}\le |E|\le C h^{-1}.
\]
Thus
\[
 \mathsf J_{P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}}(h,C_mh^{\kappa})\asymp h^{-1}. \tag{2}
\]

For the isolated density put \(s_x=d(x,x_{\star})\).  The same coordinate comparison gives, uniformly in the side \(t\),
\[
 q_{t,P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}}(x,h)\ge
 \begin{cases}
 c h^{\kappa},&s_x\le2h,\\
 c h^2\min\{1,(s_x/h_0)^{\kappa-2}\},&s_x>2h.
 \end{cases} \tag{3}
\]
Indeed, in the first case one integrates the density over a side-specific subball of radius proportional to \(h\) whose distance from \(x_{\star}\) is proportional to \(h\); in the second case, on a subball of radius \(h/2\) about \(x\), the triangle inequality bounds the distance from \(x_{\star}\) below by a fixed multiple of \(s_x\).  Since \(s_x>2h\) in the second line and \(h_0<1\), both lines of (3) are bounded below by \(c'h^{\kappa}\).  At \(x=x_{\star}\), polar integration on either side also gives
\[
 q_{t,P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}}(x_{\star},h)
 \le C\int_0^h r^{\kappa-2}r\,dr
 \le C'h^{\kappa}. \tag{4}
\]
Equations (3)--(4) prove the common polynomial lower-mass condition and the asserted two-sided equivalence at \(x_{\star}\).

If \(a_{P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}}(x,h)\le u\), (3) implies
\[
 s_x\le C\left\{h+(u/h^2)^{1/(\kappa-2)}\right\}. \tag{5}
\]
An arc of the length on the right of (5) contains at most
\[
 C\left\{1+h^{-1}(u/h^2)^{1/(\kappa-2)}\right\}
\]
points separated by \(h\).  This is exactly \(\mathrm{ass:isolated\text{-}thin\text{-}profile\text{-}upper}\), after enlarging \(C_{\mathrm{iso}}\).  At \(u=C_mh^{\kappa}\), (5) makes the upper bound constant, whereas (4) puts \(x_{\star}\) in the thin set.  Therefore
\[
 \mathsf J_{P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}}(h,C_mh^{\kappa})\asymp1. \tag{6}
\]
All estimates extend to the remaining compact range of radii by changing constants.  The circle itself satisfies \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\) by the same disjoint-arc and covering-arc calculation.  The exponent \(\kappa\) in (1) and (4) also agrees with the direct horn-volume calculation in \(\mathrm{lem:polynomial\text{-}horn\text{-}mass}\).

Finally, the assignment is sharp by the construction, the displayed potential-outcome formula implies consistency, and independence of the standard Gaussian variables gives \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\).  Both observed-side regressions and their traces are zero, hence satisfy \(\mathrm{ass:lipschitz\text{-}side\text{-}means}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:bounded\text{-}side\text{-}traces}\).  Equations (1)--(6), together with the class definitions, prove
\[
 P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}},
 \qquad
 P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}.
\]

statements.statement: For all sufficiently small \(h\), every law in \(\{\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{perv}}:0\le j\le|\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|\}\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\), the packing size satisfies \(|\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|\asymp h^{-1}\), and every pair has \(\operatorname{KL}((\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{perv}})^{\otimes n},(\mathbb P_{\kappa,k,h}^{\mathrm{perv}})^{\otimes n})\le CnL^2h^{\kappa+2}/\sigma^2\). The two laws \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,0,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,1,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) belong to \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and their \(n\)-fold products obey the same divergence bound. At an active site, their traces are \(\theta_{1,P}(x_j)=Lh/4\), \(\theta_{0,P}(x_j)=-Lh/4\), and \(\tau_P(x_j)=Lh/2\).
statements.justification: This lemma certifies the packed lower experiment inside the same classes used by the upper bounds and states its pairwise information budget.
statements.gap: Gaiffas2005Degenerate uses local univariate bumps, while the present family perturbs both identified boundary sides at many separated sites without changing the common score-mass modulus.
statements.consumer: The minimax lower theorem can invoke a concrete Fano family for pervasive thinning and a concrete Le Cam pair for isolated thinning.
statements.proof_tex:
The distance map \(z\mapsto d(z,x_j)\) is one-Lipschitz.  Thus
\[
 \psi_{j,h}(z)=(1-d(z,x_j)/h)_+
\]
is \(h^{-1}\)-Lipschitz, and each perturbed side regression in \(\mathrm{def:fano\text{-}tent\text{-}family}\) is \(L/4\)-Lipschitz.  Its absolute trace is at most \(Lh/4\le L\) for sufficiently small \(h\).  The perturbation changes neither the score law nor any local mass or packing profile.  The Gaussian-error, sharp-assignment, and consistency conditions follow from the construction.  Therefore \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\) and the two class definitions put every pervasive perturbation in \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) and both isolated perturbations in \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\).

Maximality of the \(3h\)-separated set implies that arcs of radius \(3h\) cover \(S^1\), while arcs of radius \(3h/2\) about its points are disjoint.  Comparing total arclength with \(2\pi\) gives
\[
 c h^{-1}\le |\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|\le C h^{-1}. \tag{7}
\]

Put \(a=Lh/4\).  Conditional on \(X=z\), the observed Gaussian outcome under alternatives \(j\) and \(k\) has a common variance \(\sigma^2\), and the difference of its means has absolute value \(a|\psi_{j,h}(z)-\psi_{k,h}(z)|\), irrespective of the assigned side.  For the full potential-outcome vector, the two independent coordinates contribute the same quantity and only double the bound below.  Direct integration of two univariate Gaussian densities gives
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\{\mathcal N(\mu,\sigma^2),\mathcal N(\nu,\sigma^2)\}
 =\frac{(\mu-\nu)^2}{2\sigma^2}. \tag{8}
\]
The integrand in (8) vanishes outside \(B(x_j,h)\cup B(x_k,h)\).  The coordinate calculation in the witness-membership proof gives
\[
 \int_{B(x_j,h)}f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}(z)\,dz\le Ch^{\kappa},
\]
and the isolated polar calculation gives
\[
 \int_{B(x_{\star},h)}f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}(z)\,dz\le Ch^{\kappa}.
\]
Since \(0\le\psi_{j,h}\le1\), conditioning on \(X\) in (8), and summing the two coordinates if \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}\) denotes the full superpopulation law, therefore yields, in either family,
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h},\mathbb P_{\kappa,k,h})
 \le \frac{Ca^2h^{\kappa}}{\sigma^2}
 \le \frac{CL^2h^{\kappa+2}}{\sigma^2}. \tag{9}
\]
For product laws the log likelihood ratio is the sum of the coordinate log likelihood ratios.  Taking expectation and using (9) proves
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\otimes n},
 \mathbb P_{\kappa,k,h}^{\otimes n})
 \le \frac{CnL^2h^{\kappa+2}}{\sigma^2}. \tag{10}
\]

At an active center, \(\psi_{j,h}(x_j)=1\).  The trace formulas in \(\mathrm{def:fano\text{-}tent\text{-}family}\) now give
\[
 \theta_{1,P}(x_j)=\frac{Lh}{4},\qquad
 \theta_{0,P}(x_j)=-\frac{Lh}{4},\qquad
 \tau_P(x_j)=\frac{Lh}{2}.
\]
Together with (7) and (10), these are all the asserted properties.

statements.statement: Fix \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), an assignment geometry satisfying \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\) and \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), and constants for which \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) are nonempty; \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\) supplies an explicit such specification. The two classes share the scalar lower modulus \(c_mh^{\kappa}\), but there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), independent of \(n\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), \(c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\le R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}})\le C r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\le R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\le C r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\). Thus no expected-sup minimax frontier is a functional of the common scalar modulus alone, and the frontier separates according to the declared thin-site multiplicity profile.
statements.justification: The theorem identifies multiplicity of thin locations, rather than local mass at the single worst point, as the missing information coordinate for uniform boundary estimation.
statements.gap: Gaiffas2007SharpSupNorm gives an unknown-density, spatially normalized univariate sup-norm estimator under a positive continuous design density, Gaiffas2009Uniform treats finitely many univariate density zeros, and AntoniadisPenskySapatinas2014 studies known-design global \(L^2\) loss; none gives a same-modulus isolated-versus-pervasive expected-sup separation for a two-sided causal boundary.
statements.consumer: Users of the full boundary causal trace curve can distinguish one local data desert from boundary-wide depletion before interpreting a worst-case uniform rate.
statements.proof_tex:
For a law \(P\), define the finite one-sided score measure
\[
 \mu_{t,P}(E)=P_X(E\cap\mathcal A_t).
\]
If \(P\) belongs to either class, \(x\in\mathcal B\), and \(r>0\), put \(s=\min\{h_0,r/2\}\).  By \(h_0>0\), \(c_m>0\), and \(\mathrm{ass:polynomial\text{-}lower\text{-}mass}\),
\[
 \mu_{t,P}\{z:d(z,x)<r\}\ge q_{t,P}(x,s)\ge c_ms^{\kappa}>0. \tag{11}
\]
Thus \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\).  The repaired definition of \(g_{t,P}\), the Lipschitz assumption, and the definition of the trace imply
\[
 \theta_{t,P}(x)=g_{t,P}(x). \tag{12}
\]
Under \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), sharp assignment makes \(X\in\mathcal A_t\) equivalent to \(T=t\), so all averages below have conditional observed-outcome mean \(g_{t,P}(X)\).  Consistency supplies the causal interpretation on these assignment-compatible sides; the statistical calculations use only the observed regression.

We first prove the lower bounds by subexperiments inside the same classes.  Begin with any member of the nonempty class under consideration and retain its score law and geometry.  On an extension carrying independent \(Z_0,Z_1\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), set \(Y(s)=\sigma Z_s\), \(s\in\{0,1\}\), to obtain a baseline law \(Q_0\).  Its regressions and traces vanish.  The design conditions are unchanged, while the response conditions follow directly, so \(Q_0\) remains in the same class.

For the isolated class take
\[
 h=a_0n^{-1/(\kappa+2)},
\]
where \(a_0>0\) is chosen below.  For large \(n\), \(h\le h_0/3\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:isolated\text{-}thin\text{-}site}\) and the definition of \(\mathsf J_P\) provide \(x_h\in\mathcal B\) and \(t_h\in\{0,1\}\) such that
\[
 q_{t_h,P}(x_h,h)=a_P(x_h,h)\le C_mh^{\kappa}. \tag{13}
\]
Set
\[
 \psi_h(z)=\left(1-\frac{3d(z,x_h)}h\right)_+,
 \qquad \eta_h=\frac{Lh}{12}.
\]
If \(t_h=1\), shift \(Y(1)\) upward by \(\eta_h\psi_h(X)\); if \(t_h=0\), shift \(Y(0)\) downward by the same amount, leaving the other potential outcome unshifted.  The perturbation is \(L/4\)-Lipschitz, is bounded by \(L\), preserves the score law, and preserves Gaussian errors.  Hence the resulting law \(Q_1\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\).  By (12),
\[
 \|\tau_{Q_1}-\tau_{Q_0}\|_{\infty}\ge\eta_h. \tag{14}
\]
Using the Gaussian identity (8), the support of the tent, and (13),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_1,Q_0)
 &=\frac{\eta_h^2}{2\sigma^2}\int\psi_h(z)^2\,d\mu_{t_h,P}(z)\\
 &\le\frac{C_mL^2}{288\sigma^2}h^{\kappa+2}. 
 \end{aligned} \tag{15}
\]
Additivity of relative entropy for product measures gives
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})\le Ca_0^{\kappa+2}.
\]
Choose \(a_0\) so that this is at most \(1/8\).  The two-law clause of \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}information\text{-}testing}\), applied with the sup metric and \(2\delta=\eta_h\), gives
\[
 R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}})
 \ge c n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}=c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}. \tag{16}
\]

For the pervasive class take
\[
 h=a_0\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.
\]
For large \(n\), \(h\le h_0/3\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:pervasive\text{-}thin\text{-}sites}\) supplies \(h\)-separated points \(x_1,\ldots,x_M\) with
\[
 M\ge c_Jh^{-1},\qquad a_P(x_j,h)\le C_mh^{\kappa}. \tag{17}
\]
Finiteness follows from \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\).  Choose at each point a side attaining the minimum, and perturb that side with a radius-\(h/3\), height-\(Lh/12\) tent, upward on side one and downward on side zero.  The preceding membership argument gives laws \(Q_1,\ldots,Q_M\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\).  The supports of distinct tents do not contain the other centers, so their target curves are pairwise separated by at least \(Lh/12\) in sup norm.  The calculation in (15) gives
\[
 \max_{1\le j\le M}\operatorname{KL}(Q_j^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 \le Cnh^{\kappa+2}=Ca_0^{\kappa+2}\log n. \tag{18}
\]
For fixed \(\kappa\), (17) implies \(\log M\ge c_{\kappa}\log n\) eventually.  Choose \(a_0\) small enough that (18) is at most \(a\log M\), with \(a<1/8\).  The multiple-law clause of \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}information\text{-}testing}\) yields
\[
 R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})
 \ge c\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(\kappa+2)}
 =c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}. \tag{19}
\]

We next give genuine data-driven upper bounds.  Fix \(0<b\le h_0/2\), and choose a deterministic maximal \(b/2\)-separated set \(z_1,\ldots,z_M\) in \(\mathcal B\).  It is a \(b/2\)-net, and global boundary entropy gives \(M\le2C_{\mathcal B}b^{-1}\).  Let \(j(x)\) be the least index with \(d(x,z_{j(x)})\le b/2\), and define
\[
 K_{t,j}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf1\{X_i\in\mathcal A_t,d(X_i,z_j)\le b\},
\]
\[
 \overline g_{t,j}=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^nY_i\mathbf1\{X_i\in\mathcal A_t,d(X_i,z_j)\le b\}}{K_{t,j}\vee1},
 \qquad
 \widetilde\tau_{n,b}(x)=\overline g_{1,j(x)}-\overline g_{0,j(x)}.
\]
This is one estimator measurable in the sample and known geometry.  On \(K_{t,j(x)}>0\), equations (11)--(12) and Lipschitz smoothness imply
\[
 \left|\mathbb E_P(\overline g_{t,j(x)}\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n)-\theta_{t,P}(x)\right|
 \le\frac{3Lb}{2}. \tag{20}
\]

We shall use the following elementary count calculation.  If \(N\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,q)\), Markov's inequality applied to \(2^{-N}\) and \(1-y\le e^{-y}\) give
\[
 \Pr(N\le nq/2)
 \le2^{nq/2}(1-q/2)^n
 \le e^{-nq/8}. \tag{21}
\]
For the pervasive upper bound set \(b=r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\).  Polynomial lower mass, (21), and a union bound give an event \(H_b\) on which every \(K_{t,j}\ge nc_mb^{\kappa}/2\) and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}P(H_b^c)
 \le Cb^{-1}e^{-cnc_mb^{\kappa}}. \tag{22}
\]
Conditionally on the scores and on \(H_b\), Gaussian errors and a union bound over \(2M\) averages give
\[
 \mathbb E_P\left[
 \max_{t,j}|\overline g_{t,j}-\mathbb E_P(\overline g_{t,j}\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n)|
 \mid X_1,\ldots,X_n\right]
 \le C\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e/b)}{nc_mb^{\kappa}}}. \tag{23}
\]
Since \(nb^{\kappa+2}=\log n\), the right side is at most \(C_{\kappa}b\).  On \(H_b^c\), bounded traces and Lipschitz smoothness bound every conditional mean by \(L(1+h_0)<2L\), while a Gaussian union bound bounds the conditional expected maximum noise by \(C\sigma\sqrt{\log(e/b)}\).  Combining (20)--(23) gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 \mathbb E_P\|\widetilde\tau_{n,b}-\tau_P\|_{\infty}
 \le C_{\kappa}b+C\{L+\sigma\sqrt{\log(e/b)}\}b^{-1}e^{-cnc_mb^{\kappa}}
 \le C_{\kappa}b. \tag{24}
\]

For the isolated upper bound set \(b=r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\), so \(nb^{\kappa}=b^{-2}\).  Fix a side, choose \(D\ge C_m\), put \(u_{\ell}=\min\{1,D2^{\ell}b^{\kappa}\}\), and group net centers according as \(q_{t,P}(z_j,b)\le u_0\) or \(u_{\ell-1}<q_{t,P}(z_j,b)\le u_{\ell}\).  Every center in group \(\ell\) obeys
\[
 a_P(z_j,b/2)\le q_{t,P}(z_j,b)\le u_{\ell}.
\]
Applying the isolated profile upper bound at radius \(b/2\), and the global entropy bound for the terminal group, yields
\[
 M_{\ell}\le C_{\kappa}\{1+2^{\ell/(\kappa-2)}\}. \tag{25}
\]
In group zero, polynomial lower mass makes the mean count at least \(c_mb^{-2}\); in group \(\ell\ge1\), it exceeds \(D2^{\ell-1}b^{-2}\).  Equations (21) and (25), summed over groups and sides, give an event \(H_b\) such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}}P(H_b^c)
 \le C_{\kappa}\sum_{\ell\ge0}\{1+2^{\ell/(\kappa-2)}\}e^{-cb^{-2}2^{\ell}}
 \le C_{\kappa}e^{-c_{\kappa}/b^2}. \tag{26}
\]
On \(H_b\), a Gaussian union bound at threshold \(zb\) gives
\[
 \Pr_P\left\{
 \max_{t,j}|\overline g_{t,j}-\mathbb E_P(\overline g_{t,j}\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n)|>zb
 \mid X_1,\ldots,X_n\right\}
 \le C_{\kappa}\sum_{\ell\ge0}\{1+2^{\ell/(\kappa-2)}\}e^{-cz^22^{\ell}}.
\]
The series is at most \(C_{\kappa}e^{-c_{\kappa}z^2}\) for all sufficiently large fixed \(z\); integration gives conditional expected stochastic maximum \(O_{\kappa}(b)\).  Equation (20) gives bias \(O(b)\), and the bad-event contribution is \(o(b)\) by (26) and the same Gaussian maximum bound used after (23).  Therefore
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}}
 \mathbb E_P\|\widetilde\tau_{n,b}-\tau_P\|_{\infty}
 \le C_{\kappa}b. \tag{27}
\]
The definition of \(R_n\), applied to (24) and (27), proves both upper bounds.  Together with (16) and (19), this proves both matched rates.  The explicit nonempty circular specifications are supplied by \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\), while \(\mathrm{lem:fano\text{-}tent\text{-}validity}\) independently certifies concrete legal lower families.  Since the common scalar modulus is \(c_mh^{\kappa}\) but the rates differ by \((\log n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\), the scalar modulus alone cannot determine the expected-sup frontier.

statements.statement: Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). The estimator \(\widehat\tau_n\) uses neither \(\kappa\) nor the score density. Uniformly for \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}\mathbb E_P[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widehat\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|]\le C r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) and \(R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\ge c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\). Its fallback event obeys \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}P\{\exists x\in\mathcal B,\ t\in\{0,1\}:\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)=\varnothing\}\le Cn^3\exp\{-c n c_m h_0^{\kappa}\}\), and this event's contribution is included in the expected-risk bound.
statements.justification: This closes the same-class upper and lower frontier in the pervasive polynomial regime while controlling the operational empty-admissible-set fallback.
statements.gap: Gaiffas2007SharpSupNorm gives an unknown-density, spatially varying sup-norm estimator and an inhomogeneous band for a positive continuous univariate design, Gaiffas2007PointwiseAdaptive adapts at one query point, Gaiffas2009Uniform treats finitely many univariate density zeros, and AntoniadisPenskySapatinas2014 uses known design density and global \(L^2\) loss; none handles vanishing mass on two assignment sides uniformly along a boundary with a same-modulus \(h^{-1}\)-site converse.
statements.consumer: The \(R\), Python, and Stata \(\texttt{rd2d}\) workflows can use observed-count bandwidths that widen automatically in depleted boundary segments and have a specified safe fallback.
statements.proof_tex:
The partition and sharp assignment imply \(X_i\in\mathcal A_t\) if and only if \(T_i=t\).  Inspection of \(\mathrm{def:empirical\text{-}counts}\), \(\mathrm{def:local\text{-}constant\text{-}side\text{-}fit}\), \(\mathrm{def:admissible\text{-}bandwidths}\), \(\mathrm{def:count\text{-}adaptive\text{-}bandwidth}\), and \(\mathrm{def:mass\text{-}adaptive\text{-}estimator}\) shows that \(\widehat\tau_n\) is measurable in \(\mathcal D_n\), the known geometry, \(L\), \(\sigma\), and \(n\), and uses neither \(\kappa\) nor the score density.

Fix \(2<\kappa\le\overline\kappa\), and put
\[
 r=\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), the dyadic grid contains \(h_*\) with
\[
 r\le h_*<2r. \tag{28}
\]
Take a maximal \(h_*/2\)-separated boundary net.  It has at most \(2C_{\mathcal B}h_*^{-1}\) points by global boundary entropy.  If a net point \(z_j\) is within \(h_*/2\) of \(x\), then \(B(z_j,h_*/2)\subseteq B(x,h_*)\).  Polynomial lower mass therefore gives
\[
 \mathbb E_PN_{t,n}(z_j,h_*/2)\ge nc_m(h_*/2)^{\kappa}. \tag{29}
\]
Apply the binomial inequality (21) to all center-side counts.  Ball inclusion then yields an event \(G_n\) on which, simultaneously in \(x\in\mathcal B\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 N_{t,n}(x,h_*)\ge c nc_mh_*^{\kappa},
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}P(G_n^c)
 \le Ch_*^{-1}e^{-cnc_mh_*^{\kappa}}. \tag{30}
\]
Uniformly over \(2<\kappa\le\overline\kappa\),
\[
 \frac{nh_*^{\kappa}}{\log(e+n/h_*)}
 \ge c\left(\frac n{\log n}\right)^{2/(\overline\kappa+2)}\longrightarrow\infty. \tag{31}
\]
Thus \(h_*\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)\) everywhere on \(G_n\), for all sufficiently large \(n\).  The minimizing property of the selected bandwidth, (28), and \(nr^{\kappa+2}=\log n\) imply
\[
 L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/\widehat h_{t,n}(x))}{N_{t,n}(x,\widehat h_{t,n}(x))}}
 \le Cr. \tag{32}
\]

Condition on the scores.  Polynomial lower mass puts every boundary point in both side supports exactly as in (11), so the trace identity (12) applies.  If the selected count \(N\) is nonzero, Lipschitz smoothness gives
\[
 \left|N^{-1}\sum_{i\in S_{t,x,\widehat h}}g_{t,P}(X_i)-\theta_{t,P}(x)\right|
 \le L\widehat h_{t,n}(x). \tag{33}
\]
Let
\[
 Z_n=\max_{S\in\mathscr S_n}
 \frac{|\sum_{i\in S}\{Y_i-g_{T_i,P}(X_i)\}|}{\sigma\sqrt{|S|}}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem:disk\text{-}pattern\text{-}gaussian\text{-}control}\) and \(|\mathcal H_n|\le2+\log_2n\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P(Z_n\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n)\le C\sqrt{\log n}. \tag{34}
\]
Every selected nonempty set belongs to \(\mathscr S_n\).  Since \(h\le h_0<1\) implies \(\log(e+n/h)\ge\log n\), equations (32)--(34), followed by the triangle inequality over the two sides, show that the conditional expected sup loss is at most \(Cr\) on \(G_n\).

On \(G_n^c\), a selected set comes from either an admissible bandwidth or the fallback \(h_0\).  The trace bound and Lipschitz smoothness bound the conditional mean of every nonempty fit by \(L(1+h_0)<2L\), while an empty fit is zero.  Equation (34), with \(|S|^{-1/2}\le1\), gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P\left[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widehat\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n\right]
 \le C\{L+\sigma\sqrt{\log n}\}. \tag{35}
\]
Using (30)--(35) and (31),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widehat\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \le Cr+C\{L+\sigma\sqrt{\log n}\}h_*^{-1}e^{-cnc_mh_*^{\kappa}}
 \le Cr. \tag{36}
\]
The constants can be chosen uniformly in \(2<\kappa\le\overline\kappa\), because (31) gives a common diverging lower bound for the exponential argument.

The lower bound is the pervasive construction proved in \(\mathrm{thm:thickness\text{-}entropy\text{-}separation}\), with the explicit circular family certified by \(\mathrm{lem:fano\text{-}tent\text{-}validity}\).  Choosing its scale as \(a_0r\) gives packing logarithm bounded below by a fixed multiple of \(\log n\), uniformly over the compact exponent range, while the product divergence is at most \(Ca_0^{\kappa+2}\log n\le Ca_0^4\log n\).  A fixed sufficiently small \(a_0\) and \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}information\text{-}testing}\), as used in that theorem, yield
\[
 R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\ge cr. \tag{37}
\]

It remains to verify the explicit fallback probability.  Take a maximal \(h_0/2\)-separated boundary net; it has at most \(2C_{\mathcal B}/h_0\) points.  At every center and side the expected radius-\(h_0/2\) count is at least \(nc_m(h_0/2)^{\kappa}\).  Uniformly in the exponent range, this is eventually at least \(16\log(e+n/h_0)\).  The binomial inequality (21), a union bound, and ball inclusion show that, outside an event of probability at most
\[
 C\exp\{-cnc_mh_0^{\kappa}\}, \tag{38}
\]
one has \(N_{t,n}(x,h_0)\ge8\log(e+n/h_0)\) for every \(x,t\).  Hence \(h_0\) is admissible everywhere and no fallback occurs.  Enlarging \(C\), (38) implies the stated \(Cn^3\exp\{-cnc_mh_0^{\kappa}\}\) bound.  Equation (35) and the sharper event estimate in (30) show that the fallback contribution is already included in (36).  Equations (36)--(38) prove the theorem.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(\alpha>0\), \(m_{\alpha}(h)>0\) for all \(h>0\), \(m_{\alpha}(h)\asymp h^{\alpha+1}\exp(-h^{-\alpha})\) as \(h\downarrow0\), and there exists \(h_n\downarrow0\) such that \(n m_{\alpha}(h_n)/\log n\to\infty\). Therefore a fixed exponential horn is compatible with logarithmically slow consistency and does not by itself force order-one risk.
statements.justification: This proposition removes a false early-kill premise before it contaminates the minimax theorem or the applied interpretation.
statements.gap: Gaiffas2005Degenerate obtains a logarithmic pointwise rate under severe design degeneracy; the present proposition records the corresponding boundary-modulus sanity condition without claiming a new minimax theorem.
statements.consumer: Applied analysts will not mistake an extremely thin but positive region for a formally non-estimable boundary segment.
statements.proof_tex:
Positivity is immediate from the strictly positive integrand in \(\mathrm{def:exponential\text{-}modulus}\). With the substitution \(s=u^{-\alpha}\),
\[
 m_\alpha(h)=\frac2\alpha\int_{h^{-\alpha}}^\infty e^{-s}s^{-1/\alpha-1}\,ds.
\]
Let \(a=1+1/\alpha\) and \(x=h^{-\alpha}\). Integration by parts gives
\[
 \int_x^\infty e^{-s}s^{-a}\,ds
 =e^{-x}x^{-a}-a\int_x^\infty e^{-s}s^{-a-1}\,ds.
\]
The last integral lies between zero and \(x^{-1}\int_x^\infty e^{-s}s^{-a}\,ds\). Consequently the ratio of the left side to \(e^{-x}x^{-a}\) is squeezed between \((1+a/x)^{-1}\) and one, and tends to one. Therefore
\[
 m_\alpha(h)\sim\frac2\alpha h^{\alpha+1}e^{-h^{-\alpha}}
 \qquad(h\downarrow0),
\]
which proves the claimed two-sided asymptotic order.

Choose \(h_n=(\tfrac12\log n)^{-1/\alpha}\) for large \(n\). Then \(h_n\downarrow0\), \(e^{-h_n^{-\alpha}}=n^{-1/2}\), and the asymptotic equivalence gives
\[
 \frac{n m_\alpha(h_n)}{\log n}
 \asymp n^{1/2}(\log n)^{-(\alpha+1)/\alpha-1}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Thus the fixed positive exponential modulus passes the effective-sample-size condition and cannot, by itself, imply an order-one lower bound.

statements.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\) and \(m(r)>0\) for every \(0<r\le h_0\). For every nonempty class \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-},\mathsf J_{+})\), let \(\overline\tau_n(x)=\Pi_{[-2L,2L]}\{\widehat\tau_n(x)\}\), where \(\Pi_I\) is Euclidean projection onto the interval \(I\). There are constants \(A,C,c,a>0\), depending only on the fixed envelopes, such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-},\mathsf J_{+})}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\overline\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \le C\min\left[ L,\ 
 \inf_{\substack{h,2h\in\mathcal H_n\\nm(h)\ge A\log(e+n/h)}}
 \left\{Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h)}{nm(h)}}\right\}\right],
\]
with the infimum of the empty set interpreted as \(+\infty\). The estimator in this display uses none of \(m,\mathsf J_{-},\mathsf J_{+}\); they occur only in its guarantee. Conversely, if \(0<h\le h_0/3\), \(0<u\le1\), and \(M=\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\), then
\[
 R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-},\mathsf J_{+})\}\ge cLh
\]
whenever either \(M\ge1\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\), or \(M\ge2\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\log(M+1)\). Hence a sufficient uniform-consistency condition for a sequence of nonempty such classes with lower moduli \(m_n\) is the existence of \(h_n\downarrow0\), with \(h_n,2h_n\in\mathcal H_n\), such that \(nm_n(h_n)/\log(e+n/h_n)\to\infty\); a necessary condition is that the supremum of the lower-bound-feasible values of \(h\) in the preceding display tends to zero. For a fixed positive exponential modulus \(m_\alpha\), the sufficient condition holds. With polynomial profiles, the lower display yields the isolated rate \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\) when \(M\asymp1\) and the pervasive rate \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) when \(M\asymp h^{-1}\); together with \(\mathrm{thm:thickness\text{-}entropy\text{-}separation}\), these rates are exact. For arbitrary slack lower and upper profile envelopes the two displayed bounds need not coincide, so this is a proved two-sided bracket, not an assertion of an unproved exact arbitrary-profile criterion.
statements.proof_tex:
Under the partition condition, sharp assignment makes \(X_i\in\mathcal A_t\) equivalent to \(T_i=t\).  Positivity of \(m(r)\) at every radius and \(\mathrm{ass:declared\text{-}modulus\text{-}lower\text{-}mass}\) put every boundary point in both one-sided supports by the argument in (11).  Hence the Lipschitz trace identity (12) is available.  Since the bounded-trace assumption gives \(\tau_P(x)\in[-2L,2L]\), projection onto this interval cannot increase pointwise error and the clipped loss is at most \(4L\).

Fix \(h\) in the displayed infimum.  A maximal \(h\)-separated boundary net has at most \(C_{\mathcal B}h^{-1}\) points and covers \(\mathcal B\).  If \(z\) is a net point within \(h\) of \(x\), then \(B(z,h)\subseteq B(x,2h)\).  The declared lower modulus and the binomial bound (21) therefore imply
\[
 \Pr_P\left\{\inf_{x\in\mathcal B,t\in\{0,1\}}N_{t,n}(x,2h)<\frac12nm(h)\right\}
 \le Ch^{-1}e^{-cnm(h)}. \tag{40}
\]
If \(nm(h)\ge A\log(e+n/h)\), a fixed sufficiently large \(A\) makes \(2h\) admissible everywhere on the complementary event.  The minimizing property of \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)\), the Lipschitz bias bound, and \(\mathrm{lem:disk\text{-}pattern\text{-}gaussian\text{-}control}\) then yield
\[
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\overline\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \le C\left\{Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h)}{nm(h)}}\right\}
 +4LCh^{-1}e^{-cnm(h)}. \tag{41}
\]
Choosing \(A\) larger if necessary makes the last term no larger than a constant multiple of \(Lh\).  The deterministic bound \(4L\) applies if there is no qualifying scale.  Taking the infimum over qualifying dyadic pairs proves the stated upper bracket.  The construction of the estimator contains none of \(m,\mathsf J_{-},\mathsf J_{+}\); those objects enter only (40)--(41).

For the lower bracket, take any member of the nonempty class and retain its score marginal and geometry.  Replace both side regressions by zero and put independent \(\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\) errors on the two potential outcomes.  This baseline \(P_0\) remains in the class: all mass and profile conditions depend only on the unchanged score law, while zero regressions satisfy the response conditions.

Let \(M=\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\).  Since \(\mathsf J_P(h,u)\ge M\), there are \(h\)-separated points \(x_1,\ldots,x_M\) at which one side has mass at most \(u\).  At each point choose such a side and perturb only that side with
\[
 \eta_h\psi_{j,h}(z),\qquad
 \eta_h=\frac{Lh}{12},qquad
 \psi_{j,h}(z)=\left(1-\frac{3d(z,x_j)}h\right)_+,
\]
using a positive sign on side one and a negative sign on side zero.  Positivity of \(m\) ensures that the center is in both one-sided supports, so the trace shift equals \(\eta_h\).  The perturbation is \(L/4\)-Lipschitz, has trace bounded by \(L\), and changes neither the score law nor the Gaussian variance.  Every alternative \(P_j\) therefore belongs to the same class.  At the center \(x_j\), all other tents vanish because the sites are \(h\)-separated, so the target curves are pairwise separated by at least \(\eta_h\) in sup norm.  The Gaussian shift calculation gives
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_j^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
 \le C\frac{nL^2h^2u}{\sigma^2}. \tag{42}
\]
If \(M=1\), the two-law clause of \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}information\text{-}testing}\) and the first information condition give \(R_n\ge cLh\).  If \(M\ge2\), choose the numerical constant \(a\) in the theorem small enough that \(a\log(M+1)\) is at most the multiple-law threshold in that lemma, uniformly for \(M\ge2\).  Then (42) and its multiple-law clause give the same lower bound.  This proves both alternatives in the lower display.

For a sequence of classes, if \(h_n\downarrow0\), \(h_n,2h_n\in\mathcal H_n\), and
\[
 \frac{nm_n(h_n)}{\log(e+n/h_n)}\longrightarrow\infty,
\]
then the two terms in braces in (41) tend to zero, proving sufficiency for uniform consistency.  Conversely, if the supremum of lower-bound-feasible radii failed to tend to zero, a subsequence would contain feasible \(h\ge\epsilon>0\), and the lower bracket would keep minimax risk above \(cL\epsilon\); this proves necessity in the stated form.

For the exponential modulus, \(\mathrm{prop:exponential\text{-}horn\text{-}consistency}\) gives its small-radius asymptotics.  More explicitly, taking
\[
 s_n=\{(\log n)/2\}^{-1/\alpha}
\]
gives \(ns_n^{\alpha+1}e^{-s_n^{-\alpha}}/\log n\to\infty\) and \(\log(e+n/s_n)\asymp\log n\).  Round \(s_n\) upward to the next dyadic grid point \(h_n\); then \(s_n\le h_n<2s_n\), \(2h_n\in\mathcal H_n\) eventually, and monotonicity of \(m_{\alpha}\) preserves the divergence.  Thus the sufficient condition holds.

For polynomial profiles set \(u=C_mh^{\kappa}\).  If \(M\asymp1\), (42) is bounded when \(nh^{\kappa+2}\lesssim1\), giving \(h\asymp n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\).  If \(M\asymp h^{-1}\), it is bounded relative to \(\log M\) when \(nh^{\kappa+2}\lesssim\log(1/h)\), giving \(h\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\).  The matching upper bounds in \(\mathrm{thm:thickness\text{-}entropy\text{-}separation}\) make these exact.

Finally, slack profile declarations can make the generic displays differ.  In the circular geometry, take \(m(h)=c_mh^{\kappa}\), let \(\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)=0\) below \(C_mh^{\kappa}\) and \(\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)=1\) at and above that level, and take \(\mathsf J_{+}(h,u)=\lceil C/h\rceil\) with \(C\) larger than the circle-packing constant.  The pervasive circular witness belongs to this nonempty declared class by \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\).  The generic lower profile exposes only \(M=1\), whereas (41) pays the global logarithm.  This legal triple proves the asserted possibility of a gap and explains why the result is a two-sided bracket for arbitrary declarations.
statements.justification: This theorem supplies an explicit profile-free estimator bound and a legal same-class packing lower bound for every nonempty declared class, while identifying the remaining gap as slack between the declared lower and upper profiles.
statements.gap: The two computable sides coincide in the isolated and pervasive polynomial regimes but need not coincide for arbitrary loose profile envelopes.
statements.consumer: The \(\texttt{rd2d}\) workflow can apply the sufficient count condition before fitting and can report the lower experiment as a certificate when uniform consistency is impossible.

statements.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). Put \(M_n=2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj\), let \(N=N_{t,n}(x,\widehat h_{t,n}(x))\), and define
\[
 B_{t,n}(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)+\sigma\sqrt{2\log(2M_n/\gamma)/N},&N>0,\\
 L,&N=0.
 \end{cases}
\]
Then the explicit band
\[
 \mathcal C_n(x)=
 \left[\widehat\tau_n(x)-B_{0,n}(x)-B_{1,n}(x),\ 
 \widehat\tau_n(x)+B_{0,n}(x)+B_{1,n}(x)\right]
\]
is data measurable and, for every declared nonempty triangular union \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)\), satisfies the finite-sample guarantee
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)}P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}\ge1-\gamma.
\]
In particular, uniformly over \(\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}}\), \(\mathbb E_P\sup_x W_n(x)\le C(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). Moreover, for any \(\epsilon_n\ge0\), every band with simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\gamma-\epsilon_n\) over a class containing two laws \(P_0,P_1\) obeys, for every \(x\in\mathcal B\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_0}W_n(x)\ge\frac{|\tau_{P_1}(x)-\tau_{P_0}(x)|}{2}
 \left[1-2\gamma-2\epsilon_n-
 \operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n})\right]_+.
\]
Thus the frozen assumptions yield an explicit honest global band and a computable two-law width obstruction. They do not by themselves establish the sharper uniform ratio to \(r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)\): the global calibration uses \(\log M_n\asymp\log n\), whereas \(\log\{eK_P(x,h)/\gamma\}\) can be bounded at an isolated thin site. Nor does the displayed two-law argument turn score-law total variation alone into an exact necessary-and-sufficient adaptation criterion without a same-class outcome perturbation whose full observed-law distance is controlled. This is a partial resolution of the honest-adaptation question.
statements.proof_tex:
The partition and sharp-assignment conditions imply \(X_i\in\mathcal A_t\) if and only if \(T_i=t\).  Condition on the scores, so all selected bandwidths are fixed.  Polynomial lower mass for every member of the triangular union puts each boundary point in each side support, and Lipschitz smoothness gives, whenever the selected count \(N\) is positive,
\[
 \left|N^{-1}\sum_{i\in S}g_{t,P}(X_i)-\theta_{t,P}(x)\right|
 \le L\widehat h_{t,n}(x). \tag{43}
\]
If \(N=0\), the side fit is zero and the bounded-trace assumption bounds its error by \(L\).

By \(\mathrm{lem:disk\text{-}pattern\text{-}gaussian\text{-}control}\), at most
\[
 M_n=2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj
\]
nonempty averaging sets can occur.  Its Gaussian tail inequality and a union bound imply that, conditionally on the scores, with probability at least \(1-\gamma\), every nonempty candidate set satisfies
\[
 \left|N^{-1}\sum_{i\in S}\{Y_i-g_{T_i,P}(X_i)\}\right|
 \le\sigma\sqrt{\frac{2\log(2M_n/\gamma)}N}. \tag{44}
\]
Equations (43)--(44), and the zero-count bound, show that each side error is at most \(B_{t,n}(x)\), simultaneously over \(x\) and \(t\).  The triangle inequality proves conditional and hence unconditional simultaneous coverage.  All counts and fits are measurable, the grids are finite, and the bandwidth rule has a deterministic tie break, so the displayed band is data measurable.

For the pervasive width assertion, \(\log(2M_n/\gamma)\le C\log n\).  The uniform count event and comparison scale in \(\mathrm{thm:pervasive\text{-}adaptive\text{-}frontier}\) show that, outside an event of probability \(Ch_*^{-1}e^{-cnh_*^{\kappa}}\), the selected bias plus the standard-error term in (44) is bounded by \(Cr_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\), uniformly in \(x,t,P\).  On the exceptional event it is at most \(L+\sigma\sqrt{C\log n}\); its expected contribution is \(o(r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\).  Since the constructed interval has
\[
 W_n(x)=B_{0,n}(x)+B_{1,n}(x),
\]
the asserted expected supremum width follows.

For the obstruction, fix \(x\in\mathcal B\) and let \(A_j\) be the event that \(\mathcal C_n(x)\) contains \(\tau_{P_j}(x)\).  Honesty gives
\[
 P_j(A_j)\ge1-\gamma-\epsilon_n,
 \qquad j=0,1.
\]
By the definition of total variation,
\[
 P_0(A_1)\ge P_1(A_1)-\operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n}).
\]
Therefore
\[
 P_0(A_0\cap A_1)
 \ge1-2\gamma-2\epsilon_n-
 \operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n}). \tag{45}
\]
On \(A_0\cap A_1\), the interval contains both target values, so its half-width is at least half their separation.  Multiplying this deterministic implication by the positive part of (45) and taking \(P_0\)-expectations proves
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_0}W_n(x)\ge\frac{|\tau_{P_1}(x)-\tau_{P_0}(x)|}{2}
 \left[1-2\gamma-2\epsilon_n-
 \operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n})\right]_+.
\]
This uses the total variation of the full observed experiments.  A score marginal is only a measurable projection, so its total variation cannot furnish the needed upper bound on the full distance without an additional same-class outcome construction.  Likewise, the global calibration in (44) has \(\log M_n\asymp\log n\), whereas the local benchmark may have bounded \(\log\{eK_P(x,h)/\gamma\}\).  The proved statements therefore establish the advertised global band and two-law obstruction, but not the explicitly disclaimed local-ratio or score-only equivalence.
statements.justification: This theorem gives a finite-sample honest band with an explicit global calibration and a general two-law expected-width lower inequality.
statements.gap: The local multiplicity benchmark can remove the global logarithm at isolated thin sites, and the frozen premises do not yet prove that sharper adaptation or the requested score-only equivalence.
statements.consumer: The Ser Pilo Paga replication can use the globally honest band immediately while treating local-oracle width adaptation as unresolved.

statements.statement: Let \(Q_0,\ldots,Q_M\) be probability laws and let \(v_0,\ldots,v_M\) be elements of a metric space whose metric \(\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}\) satisfies \(\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}(v_j,v_k)\ge 2\delta\) for \(j\ne k\). If \(M\ge2\) and \(M^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,Q_0)\le a\log M\), where \(0<a<1/8\), then every estimator \(\widehat v\) satisfies \(\max_{0\le j\le M}\mathbb E_{Q_j}\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}(\widehat v,v_j)\ge c\delta\) for a numerical \(c>0\). If \(M=1\) and \(\operatorname{KL}(Q_1,Q_0)\le1/8\), the same conclusion holds. These conclusions also hold for product experiments after replacing each \(Q_j\) by its product law.
statements.proof_tex:
We give the information argument, so no unlisted testing theorem is being invoked. For the two-law assertion, any estimator induces the nearest-point test \(\widehat J\in\{0,1\}\). On \(\{\widehat J\ne j\}\), the triangle inequality gives \(\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}(\widehat v,v_j)\ge\delta\). The smallest average testing error is
\[
 \frac12\int \min(dQ_0,dQ_1)=\frac{1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)}2.
\]
For any measurable event \(A\), the log-sum inequality applied to the partition \(\{A,A^c\}\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_1,Q_0)
 \ge p\log\frac pq+(1-p)\log\frac{1-p}{1-q}
 \ge 2(p-q)^2,
\]
where \(p=Q_1(A)\) and \(q=Q_0(A)\). The last inequality follows by Taylor expansion in \(p\) around \(q\), since the second derivative is \(1/\{p(1-p)\}\ge4\). Taking the supremum over \(A\) proves \(\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\le\sqrt{\operatorname{KL}(Q_1,Q_0)/2}\le1/4\). Hence the maximum risk is at least \(3\delta/8\).

For \(M\ge2\), let \(J\) be uniform on \(\{0,\ldots,M\}\), draw the observation from \(Q_J\), and put \(\overline Q=(M+1)^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^M Q_j\). The identity
\[
 \sum_{j=0}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,Q)
 =\sum_{j=0}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,\overline Q)
 +(M+1)\operatorname{KL}(\overline Q,Q)
\]
follows by expanding the logarithms. With \(Q=Q_0\), it implies that the mutual information satisfies
\[
 I(J;Z)=\frac1{M+1}\sum_{j=0}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,\overline Q)
 \le \frac1{M+1}\sum_{j=1}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,Q_0)
 \le a\log M.
\]
For any decoder, if \(p_e=\Pr(\widehat J\ne J)\), conditioning on the error indicator gives
\[
 H(J\mid Z)\le \log2+p_e\log M.
\]
Since \(H(J)=\log(M+1)\), it follows that
\[
 p_e\ge\frac{\log(M+1)-a\log M-\log2}{\log M}.
\]
This is bounded below by a positive numerical constant for \(M\ge2\) after decreasing the harmless numerical restriction on \(a\) for the finitely many smallest \(M\). Nearest-point decoding again implies \(\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}(\widehat v,v_J)\ge\delta\) on error. The displayed risk conclusion follows by averaging and then taking a maximum. The argument concerns only the laws supplied to it, so it applies verbatim to product laws.

statements.statement:
For fixed score values \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\), let \(\mathscr S_n\) be the collection of nonempty index sets
\[
 \{i:X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le h\},\qquad t\in\{0,1\},\quad x\in\mathcal B,\quad h\in\mathcal H_n.
\]
Then
\[
 |\mathscr S_n|\le 2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj.
\]
Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), conditionally on the scores, if \(\varepsilon_i=Y_i-g_{T_i,P}(X_i)\), then for every \(z>0\)
\[
 \Pr\left\{\max_{S\in\mathscr S_n}\frac{|\sum_{i\in S}\varepsilon_i|}{\sigma\sqrt{|S|}}>z\ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right\}
 \le2|\mathscr S_n|e^{-z^2/2},
\]
and the conditional expectation of the displayed maximum is at most \(\sqrt{2\log\{2|\mathscr S_n|\}}+1\).
statements.proof_tex:
For a disk with center \(c\in\mathbb R^2\) and radius \(r\), membership of a fixed point \(x_i\) is equivalent to
\[
 2c^{\mathsf T}x_i+s\ge\|x_i\|_2^2,
 \qquad s=r^2-\|c\|_2^2.
\]
Thus every disk trace is a sign pattern induced by \(n\) affine planes in the three-dimensional parameter \((c_1,c_2,s)\).  A trace realized by a closed disk can be made strict by increasing its radius by less than the positive minimum distance to the finitely many excluded points, so boundary equalities add no patterns.

Let \(A(n,v)\) be the largest number of open cells cut out by \(n\) affine hyperplanes in \(\mathbb R^v\).  Adding the last hyperplane preserves every old cell and splits at most \(A(n-1,v-1)\) cells, because the induced arrangement on that hyperplane has dimension \(v-1\).  Hence
\[
 A(n,v)\le A(n-1,v)+A(n-1,v-1),
 \qquad A(0,v)=A(n,0)=1.
\]
Induction using Pascal's identity gives
\[
 A(n,3)\le\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj. \tag{39}
\]
Restricting the parameter to genuine disks, fixing a radius, restricting centers to \(\mathcal B\), or intersecting every range with the fixed set of indices satisfying \(X_i\in\mathcal A_t\) cannot increase the number of traces.  Multiplying (39) by the two sides and by \(|\mathcal H_n|\) proves
\[
 |\mathscr S_n|\le2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj.
\]

By \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), conditionally on the scores, the residuals occurring in any member of \(\mathscr S_n\) are independent \(\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\).  Consequently, for each nonempty \(S\),
\[
 \frac{\sum_{i\in S}\varepsilon_i}{\sigma\sqrt{|S|}}\sim\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
For \(Z\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), completing the square in the exponential-moment bound gives \(\Pr(|Z|>z)\le2e^{-z^2/2}\).  A union bound, which does not require independence between the different set-indexed sums, therefore gives
\[
 \Pr\left\{\max_{S\in\mathscr S_n}\frac{|\sum_{i\in S}\varepsilon_i|}{\sigma\sqrt{|S|}}>z\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n\right\}
 \le2|\mathscr S_n|e^{-z^2/2}.
\]
Finally, integrating this tail from \(z_0=\sqrt{2\log\{2|\mathscr S_n|\}}\), and using \(\int_{z_0}^{\infty}e^{-z^2/2}\,dz\le z_0^{-1}e^{-z_0^2/2}\) when \(z_0>0\), bounds the conditional expectation by \(z_0+1\), as claimed.

sampling_model.design: Independent superpopulation sampling under a known sharp bivariate boundary assignment, with score density permitted to vanish at the boundary.
sampling_model.units: Each unit contributes \(O_i=(Y_i,X_i)\); potential outcomes supply the causal interpretation and only the realized outcome is observed.
sampling_model.treatment: \(T_i=\mathbf 1\{X_i\in\mathcal A_1\}\), with both assignment regions and their common boundary known.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment is deterministic. Each side regression is represented on \(\operatorname{supp}(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t})\); consistency supplies its compatible potential-outcome interpretation, and its unique Lipschitz trace identifies \(\tau_P=\theta_{1,P}-\theta_{0,P}\). One-sided information is measured by \(q_{t,P}(x,h)\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Observed-side regressions are estimated by local constants with count-qualified bandwidths, a fixed measurable tie-break, and the explicit fallback \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)=h_0\) when no bandwidth is admissible.

estimand_functional: \(\widehat\tau_n(x)=\widehat g_{1,n}(x;\widehat h_{1,n}(x))-\widehat g_{0,n}(x;\widehat h_{0,n}(x)),\quad \mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\Longrightarrow R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\text{ as }n\to\infty\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 4--6 give regular-density uniform estimation, inference, and a distance-estimator minimax lower bound for the boundary curve.

Theorems 1--2 give spatially varying uniform regression rates under inhomogeneous one-dimensional design, and Proposition 1 shows that isolated density zeros can permit local improvement over a naive uniform normalization.
Theorems 1--2 give pointwise minimax rates under regularly and severely varying random-design density, including logarithmically slow consistency for exponential degeneracy.
The paper constructs a local-polynomial Lepski estimator adaptive to unknown pointwise design scarcity and smoothness.

The paper constructs an asymptotically sharp unknown-density estimator with a spatially varying sup-norm normalization and proposes an inhomogeneous confidence band under a positive continuous univariate design density.
The paper combines Gaussian anti-concentration, multiplier bootstrap, and data-selected resolution levels for honest adaptive bands.
Theorems 2.1--2.2 derive honest bias-aware scalar intervals and efficiency comparisons from power-renormalized bias and standard-deviation formulas.

Theorem 3.1 gives minimax lower bounds and Theorems 6.2 and 7.1 give adaptive global \(L^2\)-risk upper bounds for univariate regression with a known design density having finitely many well-separated zeros.

tldr: The boundary target is the difference of the unique Lipschitz traces of the two observed-side regression classes on \(\operatorname{supp}(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t})\), so it is an observed-law functional even when conditional means at null boundary points are undefined. A single worst-point thickness modulus does not determine expected-sup difficulty: explicit circular designs have the same two-sided mass order \(h^{\kappa}\), but one has a single \(O(h)\)-arc data desert and the other has \(\asymp h^{-1}\) separated thin sites. The resulting nonempty classes have rates \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\) and \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\), respectively, and a count-qualified estimator matches the pervasive frontier without knowing \(\kappa\). The inference question asks for uniform coverage and expected half-width proportional to the explicit local benchmark \(r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}\) over a declared nonempty triangular profile union, with total-variation distinguishability characterizing any adaptation obstruction.

project_justification.gap: Distance-based boundary-curve theory assumes positive design density. Existing random-design sup-norm theory provides unknown-density spatial normalization and inhomogeneous bands under positive continuous univariate density, while degenerate-design theory is pointwise, univariate uniform, or global \(L^2\) with finitely many zeros. These literatures do not identify how the number of thin boundary locations changes expected-sup causal-curve risk.
project_justification.niche: A common scalar local-mass modulus treats one cusp and boundary-wide depletion as the same experiment even though a supremum sees different numbers of separated hard locations.
project_justification.fill: The project defines the target through unique Lipschitz representatives on restricted-score supports, constructs explicit symmetric circular witnesses and legal two-sided tent families, proves a same-modulus rate separation, and poses both the general frontier and a quantified honest-width problem on named nonempty classes.

related_work: CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance is the causal and writing anchor: its Introduction motivates the full boundary curve, Theorem 4 derives the regular-density uniform stochastic term, Theorem 5 supplies Gaussian bands, and Theorem 6 gives a distance-estimator lower bound. Its density and Gram assumptions exclude the thinning regimes here, so it informs rather than supplies the proposed frontier. Gaiffas2005Degenerate, Theorems 1--2 and Section 3, motivates polynomial and severe design degeneracy in a one-dimensional pointwise model; it does not furnish the project-specific uniform two-sided boundary-mass condition, and its severe case shows that fixed exponential thinning permits logarithmically slow consistency. Gaiffas2007PointwiseAdaptive, Sections 2--4, supplies an empirical-design Lepski template at one query point. Gaiffas2007SharpSupNorm, its abstract and Section 1, constructs an unknown-design-density estimator with spatially varying sup-norm normalization and proposes an inhomogeneous confidence band, but assumes a positive continuous univariate density and supplies neither vanishing two-sided boundary mass nor a same-modulus multiplicity lower bound. Gaiffas2009Uniform, equation (2.1), Theorems 1--2, and Proposition 1, is the closest sup-loss regression comparator because it treats spatially varying rates and isolated density zeros, but it is univariate and does not provide a same-modulus two-sided boundary packing separation. AntoniadisPenskySapatinas2014 studies a different global-loss problem: Section 2 assumes a known univariate design density with finitely many well-separated polynomial or exponential zeros, Theorem 3.1 gives global \(L^2\) lower bounds, and Theorems 6.2 and 7.1 give adaptive upper bounds; it does not study a boundary-indexed sup loss, pervasive thin sites, or two assignment sides. Kpotufe2011LocalDimension uses observed neighbor radii for pointwise adaptation to local ball-mass growth. The displayed global boundary-entropy condition is project-specific: every covering and chaining step in the proposed upper bounds uses only its global packing-number bound, not a local Ahlfors measure condition. ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2014Bands and ArmstrongKolesar2020Honest inform the multiplier-calibration and honest-width handles, but neither derives simultaneous local-oracle width under vanishing two-sided boundary information or the required score-law distinguishability criterion. Bull2012SelfSimilarBands concerns unknown response smoothness rather than adaptation across observable score-design profiles.
technical_internal_limitation: A scalar lower bound \(q_{t,P}(x,h)\ge m(h)\) cannot yield a sharp expected-sup lower bound without a compatible lower packing profile, and an upper theorem also needs an upper packing envelope across severity levels. The named class \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-},\mathsf J_{+})\) makes both requirements explicit. All covering and chaining steps for the closed upper bounds use only the global packing-number control in \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\); no local Ahlfors condition is invoked. For local-polynomial degree above zero, scalar mass still does not imply Gram coercivity; the closed polynomial results therefore use local constants under Lipschitz observed-side regressions.
honest_scope: The settled target is an identified contrast of unique Lipschitz observed-side traces on restricted-score supports, not a conditional expectation assigned directly at a probability-zero boundary point. The closed theorem target is the polynomial same-modulus thickness--multiplicity separation, with explicit circular nonemptiness witnesses and a matched pervasive estimator. The arbitrary-modulus minimax formula and triangular-class consistency criterion remain open. Honest thickness adaptation is posed over a declared nonempty triangular union with explicit local benchmark \(r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}\), simultaneous coverage, matching expected-width lower bound, and a total-variation distinguishability alternative. The regular positive-density regime is an external benchmark on a different model class, not a reduction of the \(\kappa>2\) pervasive theorem. A fixed positive exponential modulus remains compatible with consistency.
